Title: Preserve the token multiset
Rule: A valid WordSorting response contains exactly the supplied word occurrences.
Do not add, delete, substitute, or duplicate an occurrence.

Title: Use the registered lexical comparator
Rule: Order the words according to the task's registered lexical sorting semantics.
The expected output is determined by that comparator, not by semantic category or word meaning.

Title: Compare from the beginning
Rule: When two words differ, compare their characters from left to right until the first differing position determines their lexical order.

Title: Preserve spelling
Rule: Sorting changes position, not the identity of a word token.
Preserve each supplied token's registered spelling.

Title: Return the full sequence
Rule: The response must provide the complete sorted sequence.
A partial prefix or a statement naming only the first or last word is insufficient.

Title: Multiplicity remains binding
Rule: If the same token occurs more than once, every occurrence must remain present in the sorted output with the same multiplicity.

Title: Shared prefixes
Rule: Words sharing an initial prefix must be compared beyond that prefix using the registered comparator until their order is resolved.

Title: Duplicate tokens
Rule: Duplicate input tokens remain duplicate output occurrences.
Deduplicating them changes the task instance and is invalid.

Title: Meaning is irrelevant
Rule: Do not group or order words by semantic similarity, category, frequency, or perceived importance.
Only the registered lexical comparator controls order.

Title: Exact token identity
Rule: Do not silently rewrite a word, change its characters, or substitute a synonym while sorting.

Title: Local correctness is insufficient
Rule: Having several adjacent pairs in the correct order is insufficient if another pair remains out of order.
The complete output sequence must match the registered sorted sequence.

Title: No omitted occurrence
Rule: A lexically correct sequence of only a subset of the input is still invalid because the original occurrence multiset was not preserved.

Title: Group by early characters
Rule: A useful sorting strategy is to group words by their earliest differing characters before resolving finer within-group order.

Title: Resolve one prefix group at a time
Rule: After grouping words with a common prefix, compare the next unresolved character position within that group.

Title: Maintain a working ordered list
Rule: Insert each unsorted token into a working list at the position determined by lexical comparison with neighboring tokens.

Title: Compare only until order is known
Rule: When comparing two tokens, stop at the first character position that resolves their lexical order unless the registered comparator requires further comparison.

Title: Track multiplicity separately
Rule: When duplicates are possible, track occurrence counts while sorting so that no repeated token is accidentally dropped.

Title: Final sequence audit
Rule: Before accepting the answer, check both that the complete sequence is lexically sorted and that its token multiset exactly equals the input multiset.
